note: P1 confirmed: Canonical Workload box labelled the 1.2 s / 25 ms design budgets as "TTFT SLO" / "TPOT SLO", contradicting Table 4-1 ("TTFT budget"/"TPOT budget") and §4.3 ("1.2 s is the design budget, ≤ 2 s is the p95 ceiling"). Renamed both fields to "TTFT budget" / "TPOT budget", relabelled the tail values as "p95 ceiling", and added a box note stating pass/fail is judged against the p95 ceilings (TTFT ≤ 2 s, TPOT ≤ 35 ms), not the budgets. Scanned all 26 SLO occurrences in the chapter: no other SLO label is paired with a 1.2 s / 25 ms value.

P2 partially confirmed, premise outdated: Ch 7 now DOES carry a "Technical note — per-rank fit" that states the 99.97% figure (79.98 GB of 80 GB at 17.5 slots), but it sits under Ch 7 section 7, not §7.3 as cited, so the citation pointed at the wrong section. Ch 7 is out of my scope (chapter-04 only), so I repointed the citation by title and inlined the derivation: "(Ch 7, Technical note — per-rank fit: 17.5 GB weights + 54.48 GB KV + 8 GB runtime/NCCL = 79.98 GB of 80 GB)". Recompute check: 17.5 x 3.11296 + 17.5 + 8 = 79.9768 GB = 99.97% of 80 GB, matching Ch 7.

P3 confirmed: "The minimum GPU count for this single-request prefill deadline" read as a deployable count. Renamed to "...for this single-request prefill deadline under the stated 35% MFU assumption" and strengthened the existing post-arithmetic caveat to "...a per-request prefill-feasibility count under the stated MFU assumption — not a deployable GPU count and not a deployment recommendation." Arithmetic re-verified: 9,200 x 140 GFLOP / 1.08 s = 1.19 PFLOPS; 1.19/(0.989 x 0.35) = 3.44 -> 4 GPUs; 9,200/2,472 = 3.72 s single GPU; 9,200/19,780 = 0.465 s on 8 GPUs.
